Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2023, Question 1(c)
Binary numbers are stored in registers.
Negative denary numbers can be represented as binary using two's complement.
Complete the binary register for the denary number -78
You must show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2023, Question 2(d)
The negative denary number -99 needs to be stored in the register.
Complete the register to show the binary number that would be stored, using two's complement. Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2023, Question 2(d)
Convert the positive denary number 123 to 8-bit binary using two's complement.
Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2024, Question 8(b)(i)
Two's complement can be used to represent positive and negative binary integers.
Convert the two's complement integer 10110111 into denary.
Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2024, Question 8(b)(ii)
Two's complement can be used to represent positive and negative binary integers.
Convert the denary number 45 into an 8-bit two's complement integer.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 3(c)
10100011 can be stored as a two's complement integer.
Convert the two's complement integer 10100011 to denary. Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2024, Question 3(d)
The denary integer -32 is stored as a two's complement integer.
Calculate the two's complement integer that would be stored.
Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2024, Question 3(e)
The health value for a character in the computer game can sometimes be a negative value.
The negative values are stored as two's complement 8-bit integers.
A character has a health value of -25.
Calculate the two's complement 8-bit integer for -25. Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 3(e)
A negative binary integer needs to be stored in a register in the computer.
Give the name of the number system that can be used to represent negative binary integers.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 1(e)
Calculate the denary number for the two's complement binary integer 10001110. Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2025, Question 1(g)
The negative denary number -22 is stored in RAM.
Negative denary numbers can be represented as binary using two's complement.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for the denary number -22.
You must show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2025, Question 1(d)
The two's complement 8-bit binary integer 11001001 is stored.
Convert the two's complement 8-bit binary integer to denary. Show all of your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2025, Question 1(f)
A calculator has 8-bit registers.
The result of a calculation could be a negative denary number.
State how the calculator could represent a negative denary number as a binary number.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2025, Question 1(d)
If the owner of the shop wants to make the room very cold, she may need to enter a negative denary number.
The negative denary number could be represented using two's complement.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for the temperature -5.
Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2026, Question 6(d)
Convert the two's complement binary integer 01110101 into denary.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 1(c)(i)
One item of data displayed on the smartwatch is the current outdoor temperature. The temperature is stored in a register as a two's complement binary integer.
Show whether two's complement is a base 2, base 8, base 10 or base 16 number system. Type one letter.
A base 2
B base 8
C base 10
D base 16

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 1(c)(ii)
The outdoor temperature is stored in a register as a two's complement binary integer.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for the temperature of 32 degrees Celsius.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 1(c)(iii)
The outdoor temperature is stored in a register as a two's complement binary integer.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for the temperature of -14 degrees Celsius.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2026, Question 8(d)(i)
A display screen next to the keypad displays the current temperature inside the building.
The current temperature is stored as a two's complement binary integer and is displayed as a denary number.
Give the denary number that would be displayed for each of the two's complement binary integers.
00100011
11101010

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2026, Question 8(d)(ii)
The current temperature is stored as a two's complement binary integer and is displayed as a denary number.
Give the two's complement binary integer that would be stored when the denary number 14 is displayed.

A freezer stores its temperature as a two's complement 8-bit binary integer.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for the temperature -18.
Show all your working.

Convert the two's complement 8-bit binary integer 11011000 to denary.
Show all your working.

A weather station in a very cold place stores the wind chill as a two's complement 8-bit binary integer.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for the denary number -100.
Show all your working.

A lift stores the floor number as a two's complement 8-bit binary integer.
The lowest floor of the car park is floor -3.
Give the two's complement 8-bit binary integer that would be stored for floor -3.
Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2023, Question 2(b)(i)
A value is stored as a binary number in a register.
01111010
A logical right shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
Complete the binary register to show its contents after this logical right shift.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2023, Question 2(b)(ii)
A value is stored as a binary number in a register.
01111010
A logical right shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
State one effect this logical shift has on the binary number.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 1(c)(i)
Computers store data as binary. The binary number 10101110 is stored.
A logical left shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
Give the 8-bit binary number that would be stored after this logical left shift.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 1(c)(ii)
The binary number 10101110 is stored.
A logical left shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
Show which statement is true about the impact the logical left binary shift would have on the binary number. Type one letter.
A The least significant bits are lost.
B The most significant bits are lost.
C The number has been divided by six.
D The number stays the same.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2023, Question 2(c)
A register stores the binary number:
11100011
A logical left shift of two places is performed on the binary number stored in the register.
Complete the binary register to show its contents after this logical left shift.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 3(a)
The binary number 10100011 is stored in random access memory (RAM).
A logical left shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
Give the 8-bit binary number that will be stored after the shift has taken place.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 3(b)
The binary number 10100011 is stored in random access memory (RAM).
Show which statement about a logical left shift of two places is correct. Type one letter.
A It would divide the binary number by 2.
B It would multiply the binary number by 2.
C It would divide the binary number by 4.
D It would multiply the binary number by 4.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2024, Question 8(c)
Logical shifts are performed on binary integers.
State the mathematical effect of a right shift of four places on a positive binary integer.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2024, Question 3(c)(iii)
The character 'y' is represented by the binary ASCII number 01111001.
A logical right shift of two places is performed on the binary ASCII number 01111001.
Give the binary number after the logical right shift of two places is performed.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 3(d)(i)
A binary integer that is stored in a register in the computer has a logical left shift performed on it.
Describe the process of the logical left shift that is performed on the binary integer.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 3(d)(ii)
A binary integer that is stored in a register in the computer has a logical left shift performed on it.
State what effect this will have on the binary integer.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2025, Question 1(c)(iii)
A logical right shift of two places is performed on the binary number 10100100.
Give the binary number that would be stored after the logical shift has taken place.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2025, Question 2(b)
A logic right shift of three places is performed on the binary number 11110101.
Give the denary number for the binary number that would be stored after the logical shift of three places has occurred. Show all of your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2026, Question 6(c)
Give the 8-bit binary value after a logical binary shift left of two places is performed on the binary number 00110101.

A sensor stores a reading as the binary number 00011010.
A logical left shift of two places is performed on the binary number.
Give the 8-bit binary number that would be stored after this logical left shift.

A register stores the binary number:
11001000
A logical right shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
Complete the binary register to show its contents after this logical right shift.

A game stores a player's score as the binary number 00010111.
A logical left shift of three places is performed on the binary number.
Give the denary number for the binary number that would be stored after the logical shift of three places has occurred. Show all of your working.

The binary number 00101101 is stored in a register.
A logical right shift of one place is performed on the binary number.
Give the denary number for the binary number that would be stored after the logical shift has occurred. Show all of your working.

Logical shifts are performed on binary integers.
State the mathematical effect of a left shift of three places on a positive binary integer.

A register stores the binary number 11010010.
A logical left shift of two places is performed on the binary number.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2023, Question 1(e)
Two binary numbers are added by a computer and an overflow error occurs.
Explain why the overflow error occurred.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 1(d)
Add the two 8-bit binary numbers 11101110 and 00110001 using binary addition.
Give your answer in binary. Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2023, Question 2(e)
The number 01001100 is added to 11100011

Give your answer in binary. Show all your working.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 1(d)

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2025, Question 1(c)
Binary addition can result in overflow.
Show the correct definition of overflow in binary addition. Type one letter.
A The answer has created a negative number that cannot be represented in binary addition.
B The answer is the result of a logical shift that cannot be performed in binary addition.
C The answer is too large to represent in the number of bits available.
D The answer is too small to represent in the number of bits available.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2025, Question 1(f)
An overflow occurs when two other 8-bit binary numbers are added together.
Explain why the overflow error occurs.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2025, Question 2(a)
Two binary numbers are stored in a computer.
Add the two binary numbers 11110101 and 00111001 using binary addition.
Give your answer in binary. Show all of your working.

Give your answer in binary. Show all your working.

Give your answer in binary. Show all your working.

Give your answer in binary. Show all your working.

Explain what is meant by overflow.

Binary numbers are stored in 8-bit registers.
Give the largest denary number that can be stored in an 8-bit register.

The 8-bit binary numbers 10110100 and 10010110 are added in an 8-bit register. Overflow occurs.

Show all your working.

Each option shows two 8-bit binary numbers that are added in an 8-bit register.
Show which addition will cause overflow. Type one letter.
A 01111111 + 00000001
B 11000000 + 01000000
C 10000000 + 01111111
D 00111111 + 01000000
